# Guardrails: what each agent may touch

<!-- generated by tools/gen_agents.py from skills/setup-project/scopes.json; don't edit by hand -->

Every agent in the team runs with **least privilege**, and it isn't a request in a prompt:
a `PreToolUse` hook (`hooks/scope_guard.py`) checks every file write, every read of a
secret and every shell command the plugin's agents make, and blocks anything outside the
agent's role. If the guard can't run (no Python 3.9+), it blocks rather than letting calls
through. After every step, `taskgit.sh scope` also reverts any file the agent changed
outside its scope, including ones it committed itself. Each block is logged and shown on
the task's result card.

A project can only **narrow** these rules (`.devteam/scopes.json`, approved with the design).

## Per role

| Agent | May change | Can't change | Shell |
|---|---|---|---|
| agent-engineer | any project file | the task and state files, the design docs, raw data, frontend code, the quality gates (check.sh, lint/test configs, CI), tests, git internals, .env files | runs code and tests (no git writes, no installs) |

**One per-task exception:** on a low-risk task of a small or medium project, the Orchestrator
can let that task's coder (backend, frontend, RAG or agent engineer) write the tests too
(`taskgit.sh coder-tests`, a marker no agent can write). The gates (`scripts/check.sh`, coverage,
lint and type configs) stay closed, and the milestone's batched review reads the tests.

## Blocked for every agent

- git internals, .env files
- pushing to `main`, force-pushes, changing repo visibility, merging PRs (only the Orchestrator's
  approve step changes `main`, after your approval)
- installing packages (except env-setup), and anything that deletes outside the project
- servers or jobs left running after a step

## Bypasses found and closed

Each was found in review, fixed, and is kept fixed by a test named after its ID.

| ID | What used to get through | Test file |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | an agent committing its own out-of-scope edit kept it | `tests/test_taskgit.sh` |
| S2 | `capture.py term --cmd` ran any command | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S3 | interpreter one-liners (`python -c`, `node -e`, …) slipped past the text rules | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S4 | `xargs`, `find -exec`, `timeout`, `watch`, `parallel` hid git writes | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S5 | git options that run programs or write files, and look-alike scripts | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S6 | an unprefixed agent name could pose as one of the team | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S7 | an agent could edit the quality gate that judges it | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S8 | a write into the main checkout or another task's worktree | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S9 | package managers and one-shot runners the install rule missed | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S10 | destructive deletes other than the exact `rm -rf /` | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S11 | `gh repo edit --visibility public`, `gh pr merge` and other GitHub writes | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S12 | servers left running in the background after a step | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S13 | reading `.env` (Read, Grep, `cat`) and writing `.env.local` / `.envrc` | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S14 | no Python: the hook failed open; now it blocks | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S15 | the guard started Python for every tool call in every session | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S16 | `cd <worktree> && …` checked against the wrong folder's rules | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S17 | a `$(…)` substitution made the whole command fall back to a text scan | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S18 | visualizer and prompt-engineer owned far more of the app than their role | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S19 | a project override could drop the built-in denies | `tests/test_scope_guard.py` |
| S20 | file names with spaces or non-ASCII escaped the scope check | `tests/test_taskgit.sh` |
